run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-18T00:10:57Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The warning RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend is backed by a real, observed burst of error spans in the frontend: its STATUS_CODE_ERROR span rate went from 0 at 00:10 to 2.84/s at 00:13, peaked at 4.99/s at 00:16, was 2.83/s at 00:20 and back to 0 by 00:24 — the same magnitude as the alert's 'current: 4.422222222222222'. The frontend's error spans are its downstream calls: client grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder plus the corresponding GET /api/data and POST /api/checkout server spans (and a few tcp.connect failures); between ~00:13 and ~00:19 every frontend grpc.AdService/GetAds span was an error with zero UNSET successes. checkout also has its own error spans, on client oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge and server oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (00:15 bucket only), and frontend-proxy's own ingress/egress spans errored in the same buckets, so frontend, frontend-proxy and checkout each have their own failure evidence. Immediately before the burst, the ad and payment Deployments were rollout-restarted at 00:09:54 and 00:09:53 (new ReplicaSets whose only template difference is kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt; identical image and env), their old pods were stopped at 00:09:56/00:09:57, payment's new gRPC server logged start at 00:11:18 and ad's new container logged 'Ad service starting.' at 00:14:36. The ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config holds two switched-on fault-injection flags that name exactly these two services: adFailure (defaultVariant 'on', 'Fail ad service') and paymentUnreachable (defaultVariant 'on', 'Payment service is unavailable'); every other flag in that file is 'off'. As a hypothesis, those settings, applied to services that were restarted with a functionally unchanged pod template while no other object is seen applying a fault, are the origin of the failures; the restarts and the caller-side errors are their mechanism and consequences. The conclusion is partial: the declared faults themselves were not directly observed (ad and payment carry no error spans of their own and no error log lines were found), the moment the flags were changed cannot be established, and the ad-related error tail (~00:14:37 to ~00:23:30) outlasts the ad pod's restart unavailability, so a client-backoff or another lingering mechanism remains unresolved. ad and payment were the restarted workloads: their own error metrics stayed at 0, so I do not place them in the affected group; accounting, ad, payment, recommendation and fraud-detection showed 0 error-span rate at the sampled instants, while cart, currency, email, product-catalog, quote, shipping, image-provider, kafka, postgresql, otel-collector and load-generator returned no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series and were not otherwise checked (unknown, not zero).

claims.text: frontend's span error rate (sum of rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])) was 0 at 00:10, 0.159/s at 00:11, 2.84/s at 00:13, 3.43/s at 00:14, 4.31/s at 00:15, peaked 4.99/s at 00:16, 2.83/s at 00:20, 0.383/s at 00:23 and 0 at 00:24 and 00:25 — a real error burst matching the alert's reported value of ~4.42.

The frontend's error spans in the 00:15 bucket are specific downstream operations: client SPAN_KIND_CLIENT 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' 0.7778/s, client 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' 0.2889/s, server 'GET /api/data' 0.7778/s, server 'POST /api/checkout' 0.2889/s, client 'GET' 0.7778/s, internal 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' 0.7778/s, internal 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' 0.2889/s and client 'tcp.connect' 0.0481/s; at the 00:20 point the ad-path series (GetAds, /api/data, GET) were 0.7052/s each and the checkout-path series 0.

At 1-minute resolution, the frontend's client 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' spans were all STATUS_CODE_ERROR with zero STATUS_CODE_UNSET between 00:13 and 00:19 (error 2.1/s at 00:13, 1.3/s 00:14, 2.0/s 00:15, 1.867/s 00:16, 1.6/s 00:17, 2.1/s 00:18, 0.8/s 00:19), errors were 0.133/s at 00:11 and 0 at 00:21 when UNSET recovered to 1.633/s.

checkout has its own error evidence: in the 00:15 bucket its client span 'oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' was STATUS_CODE_ERROR 0.2763/s and its server span 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' was STATUS_CODE_ERROR 0.2763/s, both 0 at the 00:20 and 00:25 points; payment's own spans 'charge'/'grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' carried STATUS_CODE_UNSET only (0.4243/s at 00:15) and its STATUS_CODE_ERROR series stayed 0.

checkout was processing orders successfully later in the window: its log shows '[PlaceOrder]', 'payment went through', 'order placed' and 'order confirmation email sent' repeatedly between 00:16:52 and 00:16:59.

The ad Deployment was rolled out at 00:09:54: new ReplicaSet ad-5f8dd7c58d (deployment revision 2) created 2026-11-18T00:09:54Z carries pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-18T00:09:54Z with the same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad and the same env as the previous ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 (revision 1).

Kubernetes events in otel-demo show this rollout: Deployment ad 'Scaled up replica set ad-5f8dd7c58d from 0 to 1' at 00:09:54, pod ad-5f8dd7c58d-rtbj5 Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started 00:09:54–00:09:56, and pod ad-554b849958-6z62j 'Stopping container ad' at 00:09:56 followed by ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 'Deleted pod: ad-554b849958-6z62j'.

The payment Deployment was rolled out the same way at 00:09:53 (new ReplicaSet payment-5d565cf9b, revision 2, pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-18T00:09:53Z, same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment and same env), its old pod payment-55766d76b9-9fxhp was stopped at 00:09:57 and pod payment-5d565cf9b-8gwcn Started at 00:09:57.

The replacement payment container logged 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' at 2026-11-18T00:11:18.46Z, i.e. payment's serving process came up about 1 minute 20 seconds after the old pod was stopped.

The replacement ad container logged 'Ad service starting.' at 2026-11-18T00:14:36.972Z — no ad log line exists between 00:09:30 and that timestamp — and from about 00:14:37 onward it logged normal ad handling lines ('Targeted ad request received for [binoculars]', 'Non-targeted ad request received, preparing random response.') through at least 00:19:41.
Neither the ad nor the payment Deployment defines a readinessProbe or livenessProbe and neither has initContainers, so no probe-based gate is visible for these workloads.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) holds flag 'adFailure' with description 'Fail ad service', state ENABLED and defaultVariant 'on', and flag 'paymentUnreachable' with description 'Payment service is unavailable', state ENABLED and defaultVariant 'on'; both are false/off in their 'off' variant, and every other flag in the file (adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) has defaultVariant 'off'.

The ad service's own span metrics carry no STATUS_CODE_ERROR for 'oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' in the sampled window (only STATUS_CODE_UNSET, 0.1926/s at 00:15, 0 at 00:20, 0.3101/s at 00:25), and its server-side GetAds counter only grew by 19 spans between the 00:15 and 00:20 counter samples (1429 → 1448) after growing by ~280 per 5 minutes before 00:10; payment's own STATUS_CODE_ERROR series were 0 throughout.

frontend-proxy has its own error evidence in the same buckets: server span 'ingress' STATUS_CODE_ERROR 1.0852/s and client span 'router frontend egress' STATUS_CODE_ERROR 1.0741/s at the 00:15 point, 0.7642/s and 0.6978/s at 00:20, and ~0.0062/s at 00:25.

The fraud-detection container was OOMKilled (lastState.terminated.reason OOMKilled, exit code 137) and restarted at 2026-11-18T00:11:41Z inside pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-n79gv (restartCount 1), with 'Started container fraud-detection' events at 00:11:41.

Jaeger holds no traces for the incident window for frontend: the newest frontend trace returned was at 2026-11-17T23:54:30Z (source_start_at 23:54:29.69, data_as_of 23:54:30.33), about 16 minutes before the error burst, and Jaeger lists the service names 'frontend', 'ad', 'payment', 'checkout' and 'flagd' (18 services).

The switched-on fault settings in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (adFailure='on' described as 'Fail ad service', paymentUnreachable='on' described as 'Payment service is unavailable') are the origin of the two failing dependency paths: ad and payment are exactly the two Deployments restarted with a functionally unchanged pod template at 00:09:53–00:09:54, immediately before frontend's grpc.AdService/GetAds and checkout's otelldemo.PaymentService/Charge client spans began failing, and no other object is seen applying a fault to those workloads.

As an alternative for the payment path, the checkout-to-payment errors are explained by the payment pod replacement alone: payment's new gRPC server only came up at 00:11:18 after the old pod stopped at 00:09:57, and checkout's payment-charge errors are confined to the 00:10–00:15 bucket while checkout logged 'payment went through' from 00:16:52 onward.

The ad-dependent part of the frontend error burst (roughly 00:14:37 to 00:23:30) cannot be attributed to the ad pod being absent, because the replacement ad container logged 'Ad service starting.' at 00:14:36.97 and handled ad requests afterwards; a lingerin client-side gRPC reconnection/backoff after the endpoint change, or a persistent injected ad failure, is the unresolved candidate.

ad and payment themselves show no failure in their own error signals: ad's GetAds spans carry only STATUS_CODE_UNSET and payment's STATUS_CODE_ERROR series are 0, and the ad container's in-window logs contain only normal request-handling lines (a filtered query for error/exception patterns in 00:15–00:20:30 matched nothing, though that query returned no rows and is not proof of absence). The failures are therefore visible only on the callers' client spans.

The two switched-on flags do not track the error window by themselves: frontend's error rate returned to 0 by 00:24 and checkout/payment succeeded from 00:16:52, while flagd-config still read adFailure='on' and paymentUnreachable='on' when it was queried at 00:30.

The fraud-detection OOMKill/restart at 00:11:41 is not the cause of this alert: frontend's failing operations are calls to ad and checkout, fraud-detection appears in the per-service error query with a rate of 0 at every sampled point in the window (only a 0.0037/s blip at 00:05, before the burst), and checkout's own errors are on its payment call.

The frontend pod itself being restarted or broken is not supported as the cause: pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-68tcg is Running with restartCount 0 since 2026-11-17T23:37:08Z, and its error spans are concentrated on downstream client spans (AdService/GetAds, CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, tcp.connect) and the matching server route spans rather than on unrelated operations.

Check when adFailure and paymentUnreachable were set in otel-demo/flagd-config and whether flagd actually delivered the new values to ad, payment and checkout (flagd's own logs could not be read in this Run); this is the shortest path to confirming or discarding the flag hypothesis.

For the availability part of the chain, avoid single-replica rollout restarts of ad and payment during traffic (ad's app took from 00:09:56 to 00:14:36.97 to log its start, payment 00:09:57 to 00:11:18.46), and give both Deployments readiness probes and more than one replica so a pod replacement does not remove the service's only endpoint.

gaps: No trace-level evidence for the incident window: Jaeger's newest frontend trace is at 2026-11-17T23:54:30Z, and traces_search for service 'frontend' in 00:10–00:25 returned no traces, so span status codes, error messages and parent-child edges during the burst are unknown.

No frontend application logs: fetch_pod_logs for frontend-675fd7b5c5-68tcg returned 0 lines both unfiltered and filtered for 00:08–00:24 and 23:50–00:29, so the exact gRPC status/message the frontend received is unknown.
flagd's own logs returned nothing for 00:00–00:25, so I could not see when the flags were loaded or whether flagd pushed adFailure/paymentUnreachable to the services.

The moment adFailure and paymentUnreachable were switched on is unknown: no change-history integration is available and Kubernetes objects cannot prove earlier state; the ConfigMap carries no readable change timestamp.

The declared faults themselves were not observed happening (no ad/checkout/payment error text, and ad and payment recorded no error spans of their own), so the fault-injection link stays a hypothesis.

The ad-related frontend error tail from ~00:14:37 to ~00:23:30 is not explained by the ad pod restart alone; the mechanism (client gRPC backoff vs a persistent injected failure) is unresolved, and ad's server-side GetAds counter (+19 spans between 00:15 and 00:20) is inconsistent in scale with the client-side error counts.
The alerting rule for RequestErrorRate could not be read: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name='RequestErrorRate' returned no data, so the alert's exact expression and ratio are unknown.
Who or what applied the kubectl rollout restart to the ad and payment Deployments at 00:09:53–00:09:54 is unknown (the restartedAt annotation is the only trace).
Which entity produced the frontend's 'GET' client-span errors (0.7778/s) and 'tcp.connect' errors could not be tied to a named downstream from the available data.

cart, currency, email, product-catalog, quote, shipping, image-provider, kafka, postgresql, otel-collector and load-generator returned no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series; per-series absence is unknown, not zero, so they were not assessed as healthy or unhealthy.
frontend-proxy and checkout sub-resource details (endpoints, networkpolicies, resourcequotas) were not inspected; only their own span signals were read.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then.
